clue.text: One a team might sign after a break in the season?

definitions.text: One a team might sign after a break in the season?

parts.words: One a team might sign after a break in the season?
parts.note: surface reading: a player a club signs during the mid-season transfer window
setter's reading: the break is a broken bone, and teammates write their names on the injured player's leg dressing

explanation.surface: A football club recruits a new player during the mid-season break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' suggests a contract and 'break' a pause in fixtures; really the break is a fracture and the signing is autographs on the hard dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid dressing set around a broken limb is something friends and teammates traditionally write their names on.

clue.text: Is the tip rambling most succinct

indicators.note: rambling talk wanders all over the place, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A question about whether a rambling tip can really be the most concise one.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that rambling is the opposite of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithy speech is brief and full of meaning, so the superlative is a synonym for most concise.

clue.text: Affectations put on by principal or idiots

indicators.note: affectations are worn like clothing, so they are put on around the other word and enclose it

parts.note: putting on airs means behaving affectedly
a school principal is its head

explanation.surface: A complaint that pretentious mannerisms are adopted by either the headteacher or fools.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty-headed person is informally called this, a synonym for fools or idiots.

clue.text: Some upset as error is a shocker

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their run of letters is taken

parts.note: found across the end of upset, all of as and the start of error

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that an error has turned out to be a nasty surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an anagram signal, but the answer sits in plain order across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an electroshock weapon that fires barbs to stun, so it is literally a device that delivers a shock.

clue.text: Uproars after supporters originally kicked off

indicators.note: the original, opening letter is kicked out of the word that follows

parts.note: brackets are shelf supports

explanation.surface: Crowd trouble that started after the fans got things going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests football fans, but they are the wall fixings that hold up shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din or commotion, so the plural is a synonym for uproars.

clue.text: A superior criminal accomplice

parts.note: taken as written
something superior is better

explanation.surface: A high-ranking partner in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: One who aids and encourages a wrongdoer, as in the legal phrase aiding and abetting.

clue.text: Disagree with what the Thief of Time might do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to raise an objection

definitions.text: what the Thief of Time might do
definitions.meaning: second meaning, cryptic: a thief stealing from The Times newspaper would make off with an edition of it

explanation.surface: Arguing with the old proverb that procrastination is the thief of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Procrastination is the thief of time' is a proverb; read Time as The Times, whose copies are its numbered editions, and a thief would grab one.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute something is the idiom for disagreeing; literally it means grabbing a copy of a publication.

clue.text: Initially going like the wind

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word only

parts.note: the first letter of going
like and as both mean in the manner of

explanation.surface: Setting off as fast as the wind from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like the wind' reads as a simile for speed, but the phrase splits: like is the wordplay, the wind the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind in the sense of flatulence or air in the gut is informally called this.

clue.text: One fretted with a player's hand around neck?

definitions.text: One fretted with a player's hand around neck?

parts.words: One fretted with a player's hand around neck?
parts.note: surface reading: an anxious person being throttled by a sportsman
setter's reading: fitted with frets, the ridges on an instrument's fingerboard, held at the neck by the musician

explanation.surface: Someone worried because a player has a hand round their throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fretted' looks like worried and 'neck' like a throat; both are parts of a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-stringed instrument has metal frets along its neck, which the musician grips with one hand.

clue.text: Slormgorm some might say, is kind of a dog

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the compiler of this crossword
second meaning: a gun dog breed such as the Irish red one

explanation.surface: The puzzle's compiler jokes that some would call him a bit of a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword compiler is called this, and it is also a breed of gun dog, like the English or Irish.

clue.text: Performers' rights

definitions.meaning: first meaning: variety acts, each of which is called a turn on the bill
second meaning: changes of direction to the right

explanation.surface: A note about entertainers' legal entitlements.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe makes it read as performers' rights, like royalties; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In music hall a single act or performer is a turn, and turning right is a change of direction.

clue.text: One ticked off by roll put on restaurant bill

indicators.note: one item is put on, so joined onto, the other to make a longer string

parts.note: American English for the bill in a restaurant
a roll is a list of names

explanation.surface: Someone told off for adding a bread roll to the restaurant bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticked off' suggests a scolding; it means marked with ticks one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be marked off one at a time is something you literally tick off as you go.

clue.text: Tennis ear needs treatment… seriously?

indicators.note: something needing treatment is not in its proper state, so these letters must be reworked

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A player's sore ear needs a doctor, a mock-solemn query.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tennis ear' is a playful take on tennis elbow.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something with sincere intent rather than joking is an idiom meaning seriously.

clue.text: Slormgorm is mature? That's something to see!

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: I am, shortened
to mature is to grow older

explanation.surface: The setter wonders aloud whether he is now grown up, and calls it a sight worth seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so 'Slormgorm is' becomes I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture or likeness is a visual representation, something made to be looked at.

clue.text: Kent fruity types which make you go to get drugs

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE

parts.words: fruity types which make you go
parts.note: a fruit with a reputation as a laxative

explanation.surface: Kentish fruit that sends you rushing to the pharmacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drugs' looks like a noun for what you buy, but it is a verb: puts someone under with a tranquilliser.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer a calming medicine to someone is to drug them into calm or sleep.

clue.text: One scoffing with you at lame bet made in error

indicators.note: something made in error comes out wrongly assembled, so these letters need rearranging

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone mocking you for having placed a feeble wager by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffing' suggests jeering; it is the informal sense of eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining companion sits and eats at the same table as you, and scoffing is slang for eating.

clue.text: One possibly spotted in river next to tree

indicators.note: next to means the two parts sit side by side, joined end to end

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
a common tree

explanation.surface: A sighting of something by the riverbank under a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' suggests sighted; it means covered in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak of red spots on the skin is a typical example of something covered in spots.

clue.text: Dodgy opiate I injected with heroin in a state

indicators.note: something injected goes inside, so the drug letter is placed within the other letters
something dodgy is unreliable and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug user confesses to injecting a dubious opiate mixed with heroin while in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as distressed; 'a state' is the definition, a country.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sovereign nation in the Horn of Africa, and a country is a state.

clue.text: Group likely to cast Endeavour in an English city

parts.note: a gathering of witches, who cast spells
to endeavour is to try

explanation.surface: A casting agency picks actors for the TV detective drama Endeavour, filmed in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour is a British TV drama about the young Inspector Morse, so 'cast' looks like actors; here witches cast spells.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cathedral city in the West Midlands of England.

clue.text: A telegram that doesn't start with great skill

definitions.note: an adjective meaning skilled; the phrase works as a descriptive modifier

indicators.note: not starting means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a cable is a telegram

explanation.surface: A telegram written with great skill that somehow lacks an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is not a separate letter: 'a telegram' is the article plus noun, meaning a single cable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being competent or talented means having the skill to do something well.

clue.text: Small soldiers and European flipping love runners

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round, so the string is read backwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a native of Poland

explanation.surface: A squad of short soldiers and a European swearing about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping love' reads as a mild curse; really 'flipping' ends the wordplay and 'love runners' is the definition, couples who run off to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who run away secretly to marry are fleeing for love.

clue.text: Pole men turned round energy conductor of renown

indicators.note: round means going around, so one word wraps around the energy symbol

parts.note: a mast is a tall pole
E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: turned means turned back, so the word for men is read the other way

parts.note: other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A Polish man spins round with the energy of a famous conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a person from Poland; it is a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished musician, especially an eminent orchestral conductor, is honoured with this title.

clue.text: Nag raised problem with Brown and German leader

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it upward, so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a maths problem is a sum
tan is a light brown

indicators.note: the leader is the first in line, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of German

explanation.surface: A complainer brings up an issue with Gordon Brown and the German chancellor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' suggests pestering; it is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an informal word for a horse, and this is a wild horse of the American West.

clue.text: Scrap in part of church sent husband packing

indicators.note: sent, together with packing, is the idiom for dismissing someone, so that letter is sent away
completes the idiom of sending someone packing, meaning dismissing them from the word

parts.note: the area around the altar
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A fight in a church where the husband was thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a brawl in church; it is the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap a plan is to call it off, a synonym.

clue.text: Enmity in Balmoral? Heads to roll every day!

parts.note: a balmoral is a Scottish brimless bonnet

indicators.note: heads are the tops, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the first letters of roll, every and day

explanation.surface: Bitter feeling at the royal Scottish castle, with daily executions.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the royal family's Scottish castle, but a balmoral is also a Scottish cap, a convention solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense dislike or hostility toward someone is a synonym for enmity.

clue.text: Finally toga party held for a stiff gets lively

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word only

parts.note: the last letter of toga
a gathering held for a corpse before or after a funeral

explanation.surface: A toga party in honour of a dead body finally livens up.
explanation.walkthrough: A stiff is slang for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and not asleep is being lively and active, a near synonym.

clue.text: Continually preoccupied bosses I've bent out of shape

indicators.note: something bent out of shape has been deformed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An employee complains about fixated managers who keep getting upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a fixation thinks about one thing constantly, which is being preoccupied without let-up.

clue.text: Sun: "Stomach-turning Starmer is one going downhill"

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle, so the inner pair of letters are turned round

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun
the first name of UK prime minister Keir Starmer

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline sneering that the prime minister is in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, so it looks like a headline.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sliding down a slope on skis is literally travelling downhill.

clue.text: Number plate nurse found by a Spanish port

indicators.note: found by means placed beside, so the parts are joined end to end

parts.note: American term for a vehicle registration plate
enrolled nurse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nurse's car registration is traced by a Spanish harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car tag' is the US name for a number plate.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major naval port city on the Mediterranean coast of south-east Spain.

clue.text: Russian leader sends two at rear to front to get data?

definitions.note: a noun for information fed in

indicators.text: sends two at rear to front
indicators.note: the final pair of letters are moved from the end up to the beginning

parts.note: Vladimir Putin, president of Russia

explanation.surface: The Russian president sends a couple of rearguard troops to the front line to gather intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Information entered into a computer is the material it is given to work on, so a synonym for data.

clue.text: Young man with central part in 70s glam rock band

indicators.note: the central part is the middle, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: the middle three letters of Slade, the 1970s glam rock band

explanation.surface: A youngster with a key role in a 1970s glam rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy or youth is informally called this, a synonym for young man.

clue.text: State of old managers yet to get sacked

indicators.note: being sacked suggests being thrown about and upended, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The old bosses have not yet been fired.
explanation.definitionFit: The German Democratic Republic was a country that existed from 1949 until reunification in 1990.
